summary: k(y) = y_last⁻¹·C·Cᵀ with C the identity whose last column is y.

steps.claim: For y with y_last a unit, let C be the identity matrix with its last column replaced by y; det C = y_last is a unit (Cramer), so k(y) = y_last⁻¹·C·Cᵀ is invertible; for the other y put k(y) = 1.

steps.claim: The last column of C·Cᵀ is y_last·y and so is its last row (the columns of C other than the last are standard basis vectors with last entry 0); dividing by y_last gives y.
